briefdescription.para: Initialize (or reset) a protothread so it starts from the top.
Open a protothread body. Must be the first statement in the protothread function, before any PT_* operations.

detaileddescription.para: Expands to the head of a switch statement that jumps to the last saved continuation point.

briefdescription.para: Close a protothread body. Returns PT_EXITED and resets the continuation so the thread can be restarted if desired.

memberdef.name: PT_WAIT_UNTIL
memberdef.initializer: do { \ (pt)->lc = __LINE__; \ SYN_FALLTHROUGH; /* intentional Duff's device */ \ case __LINE__: \ if (!(cond)) { \ return PT_WAITING; \ } \ } while (0)

briefdescription.para: Block until cond evaluates to true.

detaileddescription.para: Each time the protothread is polled and cond is false, it returns PT_WAITING and resumes at this point on the next call.

briefdescription.para: Block while cond is true. Dual of PT_WAIT_UNTIL.

memberdef.name: PT_YIELD
memberdef.initializer: do { \ _pt_yield_flag = 0; \ (pt)->lc = __LINE__; \ SYN_FALLTHROUGH; \ case __LINE__: \ if (_pt_yield_flag == 0) { \ return PT_YIELDED; \ } \ } while (0)

briefdescription.para: Yield control unconditionally. The protothread will resume at this point on the next call.

memberdef.name: PT_YIELD_UNTIL
memberdef.initializer: do { \ _pt_yield_flag = 0; \ (pt)->lc = __LINE__; \ SYN_FALLTHROUGH; \ case __LINE__: \ if ((_pt_yield_flag == 0) || !(cond)) { \ return PT_YIELDED; \ } \ } while (0)

detaileddescription.para: Like PT_WAIT_WHILE, but returns PT_YIELDED instead of PT_WAITING, signaling the scheduler that this thread actively wants to run.

simplesect.para: Priority starvation hazard: A high-priority task using PT_YIELD_UNTIL to wait for a resource held by a lower-priority task will spin-yield every tick, starving the lower-priority task from ever releasing the resource. Use PT_WAIT_UNTIL(pt, cond) for inter-task resource contention, and reserve PT_YIELD_UNTIL for sub-tick hardware polling only.

briefdescription.para: Reset the protothread and restart from PT_BEGIN on next call.

memberdef.name: PT_SPAWN
memberdef.initializer: do { \ PT_INIT(child); \ (pt)->lc = __LINE__; \ SYN_FALLTHROUGH; \ case __LINE__: \ if ((func) < PT_EXITED) { \ return PT_WAITING; \ } \ } while (0)

briefdescription.para: Spawn a child protothread and block until it exits.

detaileddescription.para:
pt
Parent protothread.
child
Child protothread (SYN_PT struct).
func
Expression that calls the child's function, e.g. child_func(&child_pt).
The func expression is evaluated on EVERY scheduler poll until the child exits. Never pass expressions with side-effects (e.g. counter++, function calls that modify state). Pre-evaluate arguments before calling PT_SPAWN.
Usage: staticSYN_PTchild_pt; PT_SPAWN(pt,&child_pt,child_func(&child_pt));

memberdef.name: PT_DELAY_MS
memberdef.initializer: do { \ *(target) = syn_port_get_tick_ms() + (uint32_t)(ms); \ if (*(target) == 0) { \ *(target) = 1; /* 0 is the "no deadline" sentinel */ \ } \ PT_WAIT_UNTIL(pt, (int32_t)(syn_port_get_tick_ms() - *(target)) >= 0); \ *(target) = 0; /* consume — stale deadlines wrap to "future" */ \ } while (0)

detaileddescription.para: Requires a uint32_t variable to store the deadline. When used with the scheduler, pass &(task)->delay_until. For standalone use, pass any persistent uint32_t *.

simplesect.para: The target is reset to 0 (the scheduler's "no deadline pending" sentinel) once the delay completes. A deadline left in place would read as "in the future" again after the tick counter advances 2^31 ms (~24.8 days) past it, freezing the task. A computed deadline of exactly 0 (tick wrap) is nudged to 1 so it cannot alias the sentinel.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to a uint32_t that will hold the deadline tick.

briefdescription.para: Convenience form for use with the scheduler's SYN_Task (milliseconds).
Non-blocking sub-millisecond delay for us microseconds.

detaileddescription.para: Requires a user-supplied persistent uint32_t variable (e.g., static uint32_t us_target;). Does not modify SYN_Task.delay_until to avoid corrupting the millisecond scheduler timebase.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to a uint32_t variable holding the microsecond deadline.

briefdescription.para: Defer to all ready tasks, regardless of priority.

detaileddescription.para: Unlike PT_YIELD (which only round-robins among equal-priority tasks), this macro allows any lower-priority ready task to run before this task is scheduled again. The task is skipped for exactly one scheduler pass.
Use this when a high-priority task has no immediate work but doesn't want to commit to a timed delay.

memberdef.name: PT_BLOCK_EVENT
memberdef.initializer: do { \ (task)->wait_event = (SYN_EventFlags *)(grp); \ (task)->wait_mask = (mask); \ (task)->state = (uint8_t)SYN_TASK_BLOCKED; \ PT_YIELD(pt); \ uint32_t _syn_evt_matched = (task)->wait_mask; \ if (_syn_evt_matched != 0) { \ syn_event_flags_clear((SYN_EventFlags *)(grp), _syn_evt_matched); \ } \ (task)->wait_mask = 0; \ } while (0)

briefdescription.para: Block until ANY bit in mask is set in the event group.

detaileddescription.para: Unlike PT_WAIT_EVENT (which polls every scheduler pass), this macro sets the task state to BLOCKED. The scheduler skips the task entirely until the event fires, saving CPU and enabling proper tickless sleep.
Matched flags are auto-cleared after the task resumes.

simplesect.para: The clear runs after PT_YIELD returns (i.e. after the scheduler has already detected the flags during its scan), so it is safe for the scheduler to use the flags as a wakeup condition.

parameterdescription.para: Bitmask of event flags to wait for (any of them).

memberdef.name: PT_BLOCK_EVENT_WITH_TIMEOUT
memberdef.initializer: do { \ (task)->wait_event = (SYN_EventFlags *)(grp); \ (task)->wait_mask = (mask); \ (task)->delay_until = syn_port_get_tick_ms() + (uint32_t)(timeout_ms); \ if ((task)->delay_until == 0) { \ (task)->delay_until = 1; /* 0 is the no-deadline sentinel */ \ } \ (task)->state = (uint8_t)SYN_TASK_BLOCKED; \ PT_YIELD(pt); \ (task)->delay_until = 0; \ uint32_t _syn_evt_matched = (task)->wait_mask; \ if ((out_flags) != NULL) { \ *(out_flags) = _syn_evt_matched; \ } \ if (_syn_evt_matched != 0) { \ syn_event_flags_clear((SYN_EventFlags *)(grp), _syn_evt_matched); \ } \ (task)->wait_mask = 0; \ } while (0)

briefdescription.para: Block task execution (SYN_TASK_BLOCKED) until ANY bit in mask is set OR timeout_ms milliseconds elapse.

detaileddescription.para: Combines event-flag blocking with millisecond deadline tracking. The task is skipped by the scheduler until either the event fires or the timeout deadline passes.
Matched event flags are captured into out_flags (if non-NULL) and auto-cleared ONLY if the event actually fired before the timeout. Check *out_flags != 0 to determine if the event fired vs timed out.

parameterdescription.para: Bitmask of event flags to wait for.
Pointer to uint32_t receiving matched flags (or 0 on timeout).

memberdef.name: PT_BLOCK_CONDITION

detaileddescription.para:
This macro does NOT poll cond on each scheduler tick. Once the task yields as BLOCKED, the scheduler skips it entirely. The condition is only re-evaluated when the task is explicitly woken by an ISR or driver calling syn_task_resume(task).
For polled condition blocking, use PT_WAIT_UNTIL(pt, cond) instead. For event-flag-driven blocking, use PT_BLOCK_EVENT(pt, task, grp, mask).
Check if a protothread is still running (has not exited).
Check if a protothread has not yet started or has been reset.
Thread is blocked (condition not yet met)

Thread ran to PT_END — normal completion
Thread was explicitly ended via PT_EXIT

briefdescription.para: Return value from a protothread function.
Protothreads — stackless cooperative coroutines for C.

detaileddescription.para: Protothreads provide lightweight, cooperative multitasking without requiring a separate stack per thread. Each protothread is a normal C function that uses macros to save and restore its execution position via the switch/__LINE__ continuation trick (Duff's device).
A protothread costs 2 bytes of RAM (the continuation variable).

listitem.para: You cannot use a bare switch statement inside a protothread body (use if/else if chains instead).
Local variables are NOT preserved across yield/wait points. Store persistent state in static variables, globals, or a struct passed via the task's user_data pointer.
A protothread must reside entirely within a single function.
